- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% in early horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% in early horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > 2.0), model frequently overcorrects with exaggerated downward moves; cap downward corrections at 1.5x the prior peak.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in medium-term (14–28d) forecasts; if forecast is >1.5x recent high, apply downward adjustment proportional to sentiment volatility.
- In high-sentiment periods, model tends to lag true price movements by 3–5 days; shift forecast horizon slightly forward by 1–2 days for next 7d window.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model overfits to recent peaks; dampen forecast by 15–25% for 10–14d horizon.
